deck: INSIDERS WITH DOCUMENTS WIN: SEALED COMPLAINTS, WRITTEN DISCLOSURES, AND 15 TO 30 PERCENT RELATOR SHARES
CASE SCREENS BUILT ON $10 MILLION DAMAGES FLOORS, FIRST-TO-FILE TIMING, AND STRICT SILENCE DISCIPLINE
site_ui.lead: Insider relators who stay silent, gather documents lawfully, and file a sealed complaint through experienced counsel turn a lie connected to a federal dollar into treble damages, per-claim penalties, and a 15 to 30 percent share of the government's recovery.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 166 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies, with every claim carrying timestamped inline attribution to its source channel and video. Coverage runs from False Claims Act origins and relator intake through the qui tam lifecycle, data-mined DOJ enforcement, healthcare, contractor, customs, and relief-loan fraud, and the SEC and IRS whistleblower programs.

flow: No press, public posts, or comment-section questions; public information kills original-source status and invites a first-to-file block
Answer what you did, what you knew, and when; masterminding, profiting, or delaying the report drastically reduces the award
Photograph documents instead of removing them, confirm lawful access, and skip AI summaries before calling counsel
Confirm the payer would refuse to pay for the defect, tie it to government money, and plead who, what, when, where, and how
Serve the written disclosure statement with all material evidence before filing, pleading the full 10-year window and parallel state claims
The seal starts at 60 days and renews 6 months at a time; DOJ averages about 11 months to decide intervention
